sop_nsi_001.title: No Sweat Intro (NSI) — Sales Floor SOP

flow.summary: Full step-by-step process for conducting a No Sweat Intro: greeting, finding the deep why, explaining CrossFit, confirming the 10/10, gym tour, pricing conversation, objection handling, and sign-up.

steps.text: STEP 1 — GREETING: Greet them by name at the door. Ask: 'Hey, what brings you in today?'
Did they give a clear goal?
Follow up with 'Why?' and keep digging until you reach the real pain point.
STEP 2 — DEEP WHY: Keep asking 'Why?' until you reach the real pain point. Validate it and share social proof — a story of a member with the same pain point and how we helped them.
Did they ask what CrossFit is?
STEP 3 — EXPLAIN CROSSFIT: Coaching-first facility, functional fitness, scalable to every person. They came here for a human coach, not amenities. Tie it back to their why.
STEP 4 — CONFIRM THE 10/10 (before the tour): State their goal back to them. Ask: 'If we got you [their goal] in the next 90 days, would that be a 10 out of 10 experience?'
Did they say yes?
Move to gym tour.
Ask: 'What would make it a 10 out of 10? What would have you telling all your friends or staying here forever?' Repeat it back, confirm, then move to tour.

STEP 5 — GYM TOUR: Walk through PT side, back alley (lockers, cubbies, bathrooms, showers), recovery equipment, water fountain, snacks, group class floor. End with: 'Any questions? Alright — lets go talk pricing.'

STEP 6 — PRICING (Office): Set chairs turned toward the door. Open with: 'Based on what we talked about, here is what I recommend.' Choose package based on their goal and schedule. Walk through 90-day roadmap. Close with: 'How does that sound — are you ready to get started?'
Did they say yes?

OBJECTION — Spouse/Partner: Ask if they talked beforehand. Offer to step out so they can call right now. If yes after call — proceed. If no — schedule a callback. OBJECTION — Price: Ask what range works. Scale down package. If under $100 refer to CrossFit Drive. Re-close: 'With all that said — what is stopping us from getting you signed up today?'

STEP 8 — SIGN UP: Open Wodify and Lead Machine. Create athlete profile. Add PT membership first (full bundle price in PT line, CrossFit = $0). Walk through agreements. Collect payment. Schedule first PT session. Add CrossFit membership. Post sign-up: New Athlete Alert in Slack, add to Check-In List, Affinity Sheet, On-Ramp List.

flow.summary: 6 rules: Personal service rule, proactive CALM framework, use highest communication level available, active listening, next date strategy, nourishing sequences for leads.

steps.text: RULE 1 — Personal Service: Know clients friends, family, work, and hobbies. Connect every session to their life. Ask: How can I provide a 10/10 experience for you?

RULE 2 — Proactive Engagement (CALM): When something goes wrong use Clarity (explain what happened), Assurance (you have it handled), Leadership (make a decision), Movement (tell them whats next). Never go quiet.
RULE 3 — Highest Communication Level: In person > video call > phone call > voice note > text > email. Never email what can be a call. Escalate to higher channel for any issue.
RULE 4 — Active Listening: Make consistent eye contact. Put phone away. Reflect back what they say. Ask questions to understand. Be curious, not judgmental.
RULE 5 — Next Date Strategy: Every conversation ends with the next one scheduled — a specific date and time, not lets catch up soon.

RULE 6 — Nourishing Sequences: A lead who said no today is a future client. Go high frequency early, taper over time, never go to zero. Personal check-ins at 6 months convert leads that automation never will.

steps.text: Is the friend interested in becoming a member?

Ask: Is there a Bring a Friend day coming up? Lets find the best way to get them in. If no good option exists, the friend cannot join. Notify the General Manager.

flow.summary: Cancellation accepted via form, email (vegvisircrossfit@gmail.com), or text (713-715-1440). PT: stop auto-renew at end of period. CrossFit: generate next membership, stop auto-renew on second month end, prorate current month. Confirm via Lead Machine text.

sop_new_member_account_001.title: Creating a New Member Account — Protocol

flow.summary: app.wodify.com > Athletes > New Athlete. Enter first name, last name, email, and phone from Lead Machine profile. Save. Then proceed to appropriate membership SOP.

steps.text: Go to app.wodify.com and log in with your admin credentials. Go to Athletes > New Athlete (top right).
Enter their first name, last name, email, and phone number (pull from Lead Machine profile or confirm with them). Always confirm their first name — it goes a long way in making them feel welcome.

flow.summary: Push black clasp down to adjust height. Feed strap against the teeth. Tuck excess strap in containment strap. Test by putting weight on the ring — if it moves, re-feed.

steps.text: Find the black clasp on the strap. Push the clasp down. Move the strap up or down to desired height. Make sure strap is fed against the teeth so it does not slide.
Unsure if secured correctly?
Put weight on the ring. If the ring starts to move, it is fed through the wrong way. Re-feed and try again.
Fold up any excess strap and tuck it within the containment strap. Excess strap should never be left hanging or on the floor.

flow.summary: Every 6 months: open casing with Phillips head, remove damper side panel, blow out all debris with pressurized air or leaf blower, reassemble.

steps.text: Every 6 months: use a Phillips head screwdriver to open the rower casing. Remove the side panel with the damper on it.
Use a pressurized air can or leaf blower to blow out all dust, dirt, and debris from inside.
Reassemble the casing and tighten all screws.

flow.summary: Tools from gray first aid cabinet top shelf: 30in box, 3 towels, snap lock pliers (blue handles), 3-in-1 oil. Disassemble sleeve in order, clean shaft, oil with hands (not towel), reassemble in reverse. Leave flat 24 hours.

steps.text: Gather tools from top shelf of gray first aid cabinet: 30 inch plyo box, 3 gym towels, snap lock pliers (blue handles, gray square bottom, set to close), 3-in-1 oil (white and red bottle).

DISASSEMBLY (lay parts on box in order): Use snap lock pliers to remove first O-ring. Tap out the coin. Remove second O-ring. Remove thin metal ring. Remove two half-moon rings from groove. Remove thick ring. Slide sleeve off.
Use a towel to wipe down the barbell shaft — remove all chalk and debris.
Apply 3-in-1 oil directly to the barbell shaft. Use your HANDS (not a towel) to work oil in evenly — towels absorb the oil.

REASSEMBLY (reverse order): Slide sleeve back on. Place thick ring. Insert two half-moon rings into groove. Set thin ring inside thick ring. Press on first O-ring. Replace coin. Press on second O-ring.
Confirm the sleeve spins freely. Repeat full process on the other end of the barbell.
Leave flat for 24 hours in the gun rack on PT side or in the boneyard (underneath Gauntlet signs next to the office).

flow.summary: Chalk or sweat buildup is the cause. Set aside against the wall under Gauntlet signs and notify Kidd.

steps.text: Set the barbell aside against the wall under the Gauntlet signs next to the office.
Notify the owner (Kidd) that it needs maintenance. Refer to Barbell Maintenance SOP for the full procedure.

flow.summary: All tools are in the large basket on the 3rd shelf of the storage closet. Must be returned after use.

steps.text: Go to the storage closet. Find the 3rd shelf. Look for the large basket full of tools. Return all tools to this basket immediately after use.

sop_child_dog_injury_001.title: Child or Dog Injured in the Gym — Protocol

flow.summary: Look for a doctor. If none, provide first aid with consent. Children must be in the childrens area or blue chairs. Dogs must be tied to the rig next to their owner, away from weights.

steps.text: PREVENTION: Children must be in the childrens area next to the front desk or in the blue chairs by the entrance. Dogs must be tied to a floor-bolted sturdy object (such as the rig), next to their owner, away from all weights and barbells.
Look for a doctor in the gym immediately.
Is a doctor present?
Doctor takes over. Keep the class running on the opposite side of the gym.
Is the injured party a child?
Ask the parent for consent before touching or treating the child.
Did the parent give consent?
Follow same emergency procedure. Contact the owner if the dogs owner is not present.
Perform CPR or first aid following Red Cross CPR Call-Check-Care protocol. Refer to Emergency Situations SOP if needed.
Step back and allow the parent to handle it. Do not provide care without consent.

flow.summary: Try plunger first (mens restroom, first stall). If stuck, use dish soap and hot water, place Out of Order sign, retry later. If backed up all the way, call GM immediately.

steps.text: Get the plunger from the mens restroom, first stall on the left. Attempt to plunge the clog clear.
Did plunging clear the clog?
Pour dish soap and hot water into the toilet. Let it sit and drain. Place an Out of Order sign on the stall door. Return once drained and attempt to flush again.
Is the toilet backed up all the way?
Done.
Do not attempt further fixes. Call the General Manager immediately. GM will arrange for a professional to fix it.

flow.summary: Coach at end of day takes towels home, washes and dries, folds, and submits a $15 invoice to cover time and supplies.

flow.summary: First aid kit in gray cabinet behind group training wall. Ask for consent before helping. Help them make a plan for next steps (no diagnosing). Notify owner and all coaches in Slack general channel.

Ask the person: Are you okay with me helping you with first aid? If yes, assist. If no, step back and let them handle it — do not push.
Help them make a plan for next steps (do not diagnose): Are you going to see your doctor or someone else about this? Make sure they have a path forward.
Notify the owner (Kidd) and all coaches in the General channel on Slack. Include what happened and where.

flow.summary: Call for a doctor. If none, follow Red Cross Call-Check-Care. If unconscious, call 911 (5701 Almeda Rd). First aid kit in gray cubby behind group training wall. Keep class running on opposite side. Notify Kidd when person is stable.

steps.text: Ask loudly: Is there a doctor in the room?
Is a doctor present?
Doctor takes over first aid. You keep the class running on the opposite side of the gym.

Have someone else call 911 immediately. Address: 5701 Almeda Road, Houston TX 77098.
Approach the person. Tap their shoulder. Say [Name], can you hear me? If unresponsive, assume consent and begin first aid. If responsive, ask: Can I provide care for you?
Did they give consent (or are they unresponsive)?

First aid kit: red suitcase on the gray shelf in the cubby area behind group training wall (between bathrooms and that wall). Additional supplies in a clear tub surrounding the red kit. Perform first aid until first responders arrive or someone more qualified takes over.
Step back. Do not provide care without consent.

sop_out_of_stock_001.title: Out of Stock Items — Reporting Protocol

flow.summary: Report in Supplies & Repairs Slack channel, notify Rob (Member Engagement Coordinator), and notify Kidd (owner).

steps.text: Report it in the Supplies & Repairs channel on Slack. Notify the Member Engagement Coordinator (Rob) directly. Notify the Owner (Kidd) directly.

flow.summary: Must be done with another person. Ladder from supply closet, tape measure from tool drawer (3rd shelf), duct tape. Mark 10 feet and 15 feet with one rotation each. Rope must be directly in front of you on ladder — never to the side.

steps.text: ALWAYS do this with another person present — never alone.
Get the ladder from the supply closet. Tape measure is in the tool drawer (3rd shelf, tall shelving on the left, closest side of supply closet). Bring a roll of duct tape.
Set the ladder to a fully extended, stable height. Position it so the rope is DIRECTLY IN FRONT of you — never to the side (rope to the side can push you off and topple the ladder).
Climb up to the rope. Use the tape measure to find 10 feet. Wrap one full rotation of duct tape at the 10-foot mark.
Measure up to 15 feet. Wrap one full rotation of duct tape at the 15-foot mark. Confirm both pieces of tape are secure before coming down.
Return ladder and tools to the supply closet.

flow.summary: Estimated 2-3 hours. Order: trash, showers, bathroom floors (Fabuloso), toilets (Clorox), restock TP and paper towels, sinks (Lysol), mirrors (Windex), gym floor (blow out first then mop), equipment returns. Supplies on bottom shelf of supply closet.

steps.text: Cleaning supplies: bottom shelf or 2nd to bottom shelf of the supply closet.
1. Empty all trash cans (refer to Trash Bag Replacement SOP).
2. Clean all shower stalls (refer to Shower Cleaning SOP).
3. Mop bathroom floors with Fabuloso diluted in mop bucket. Wring mop until just slightly damp.
4. Scrub all toilets with Clorox wipes until pearl white. Flush after cleaning to prevent blue ring stains.
5. Refill all toilet paper (from bathroom cabinets). Refill all paper towel holders (refer to Paper Towel Refill SOP).
6. Scrub all sinks with Lysol until pearl white.
7. Clean all bathroom mirrors with Windex until streak-free.
8. Blow out all dust bunnies first (refer to Leaf Blower SOP), then mop the gym floor.
9. Return all equipment to correct locations (refer to Dumbbell Storage SOP and other storage SOPs).

flow.summary: Shower cleaner spray bottle from supply closet. Ask anyone to move personal items. Spray entire shower, wipe clean. If mildew or mold on drywall, scrub and report to GM.

steps.text: Get shower cleaner spray bottle from supply closet. Ask anyone in the shower area to temporarily move their personal items.
Spray down the entire shower — walls, floor, and all surfaces. Wipe down all sprayed surfaces. Floor and walls should appear white and clear with no dog hair, crumbs, or residue.
Is there mildew or mold forming on the drywall next to the shower?
Spray the affected area with shower cleaner. Scrub thoroughly until removed. Report to the General Manager or Kidd (owner) — even if you got it out, they need to know.
Done.

sop_leaf_blower_001.title: Leaf Blower / Gym Dust Removal — Protocol

flow.summary: Fully charged Greenworks battery. All fans off and doors closed. Start PT side, blow toward group side. Left-right-left patterns, blow off all tops. Open garage door, blow everything out. Blow down catwalk to street.

steps.text: Confirm Greenworks battery is fully charged. Turn off all fans. Close all doors.

Start on the PT side with all doors closed. Blow all dust and dog hair toward the main group training side. Work in left-to-right then right-to-left patterns, moving forward in small one-foot increments.
Blow dust off the top of ALL surfaces: wall balls, food/snack stand, water fountain, plate racks, dumbbells, and anything else with a flat top.
Continue same pattern on the group training side. Work all dust toward the garage door end of the gym. Blow off tops of all equipment on this side as well.
Open the garage door. Blow all remaining dust and debris out through the garage door. Close the garage door once clear.
Walk outside. Blow down the catwalk and ramp. Push everything all the way out to the street.

flow.summary: Excess water = clogged vacuum hose (remove and clear). Too much water = clogged filter (remove, wash, dry, reinstall). Cord yanked out = reconnect black wire. Not comfortable with electronics? Call GM.

steps.text: Is the scrubber leaving excess water on the floor?
The vacuum hose is clogged (usually dog hair). Remove the hose, pull out the clog, reattach. Lower the squeegee and test.
Is the scrubber pushing out too much water?
Filter is clogged. Open the main hatch in the middle. Find and remove the vacuum-style filter. Wash in the sink. Allow to fully dry before reinstalling.
Has the power cord been yanked out?
Are you comfortable working with electronics?
No common issue identified — contact GM or Kidd for assistance.
Reattach the black wire to its connector and put the casing back together.
Do not attempt the repair. Notify the General Manager or Kidd and they will get it fixed.

flow.summary: Blow dry gym first. Fill front hopper with 20L water + rubber floor cleaner (2nd shelf supply closet). Start switches left > middle > right. Hold both handle buttons. Squeegee down. Down-and-back patterns. Empty dirty water into mop sink when done. Store completely empty.

steps.text: ALWAYS blow dry the gym before using the scrubber (refer to Leaf Blower SOP).
Fill the front water hopper with approximately 20 liters of water (check level using clear tube on left side near handles). Add a full pack of rubber floor cleaner (2nd shelf of supply closet).
Confirm the brush is installed and the outer skirt is in place.
START SEQUENCE (exact order): Left switch > Middle switch > Right switch. Hold down both handle buttons simultaneously. Confirm the squeegee at the back is DOWN.
Clean in down-and-back patterns through the middle. Get inside the rigs as much as possible. Avoid black pipe equipment. Once per month: pull out bikes and rowers to clean behind them.

EMPTY DIRTY WATER: Unplug the machine. Take dirty water hose to the mop sink. Remove from bracket. Drain all dirty water. Rinse bucket with clean water. Reattach hose. Do not leave dirty water in machine — it will smell.
Take scrubber outside and empty any remaining clean water into the parking lot drain.
Walk it back into the supply closet. Remove the brushes and set aside. Lift the squeegee up. Store completely empty.

flow.summary: Open only when outside temperature is between 50F and 80F. Always okay to open temporarily for cleaning.

steps.text: Is the outside temperature between 50F and 80F?
Garage door may be opened.
Is the door being opened temporarily for cleaning purposes only?
Opening is allowed for cleaning regardless of temperature.
Keep the garage door closed.

flow.summary: Undo chain keeper, lower door slowly hand over hand, kick both door locks in, wrap chain clockwise around both hooks with return chain in the middle.

steps.text: Undo the chain keeper. Lower the door slowly hand over hand — do not let it drop.
Once the door rests on the ground, kick both door locks into place.
Wrap the chain back around the chain keeper in a clockwise direction. Keep the return part of the chain in the middle. Wrap around both hooks.

flow.summary: Kick open both door locks, unwrap chain, pull hand over hand until fully locked at top, secure chain clockwise around both hooks with return chain in the middle.

steps.text: Kick open the door locks on both sides at the bottom of the door. Unwrap the chain from the chain keeper.
Pull the chain hand over hand to raise the door until it reaches its full locked-out position at the top.

Secure the chain back on the chain keeper: place the return side (tension side) into the keeper first. Run chain through the middle of the two hooks. Wrap clockwise over one chain link over each hook.
